• The geyser contains a heating element, usually made of a metal such as copper, which is immersed in the water tank.
 
• When the geyser is switched on, an electric current flows through the heating element, causing it to become very hot.
 
• The heating element transfers this heat to the water surrounding it, and over time, the water temperature rises until it reaches the desired temperature.
 
• The heating element in the geyser is made of a material with high electrical resistance, meaning that it resists the flow of electricity through it. As a result, when current flows through the heating element, it encounters resistance, which causes the element to heat up.

questions.question: If 19 November 2005 is a Saturday, then what will be the day of the week on 23 November 2008?
questions.solution:
19 November 2005 is a Saturday.

Consider a regular year of days 365 as we know there are 52 weeks in a year. On consideration, each week has 7 days so there will total (52*7) = 364 days. That means if we started counting from Monday as 1st day then the 364th day will be Monday. The remaining day of the year will add up to the next day of the week from where we started, i.e., it will be Tuesday. That remaining day is called an odd day. 

A **normal year** has **1 odd day,** whereas a** leap year** has **2 odd days**.

So, 2006 = 1 odd day

2007 = 1 odd day

2008 = 2 odd day (Leap year)

Total number of odd days = 1 + 1 + 2 = 4

Saturday + 4 days = Wednesday.

19 November 2008 will be ‘Wednesday’.

Now in question we have asked about 23 November 2008

23 -19 = 4 (days)

Wednesday + 4 = Sunday

Hence, the correct answer is “Sunday”.

• Prime Factorization

Prime factorization of 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3

Prime factorization of 48 =** **2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3

Prime factorization of 120 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 5

Prime factorization of 300 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 × 5

L.C.M of 36, 48, 120, and 300 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 × 5 = 3600

questions.question: What are the group numbers of halogens and carbon family, respectively, in the modern periodic table?

• Bromine (Br)
 
• Iodine (I)
 
• Astatine (At)
 
• Tennessine (Ts)
 
 
 
• Halogens are nonmetals.
 
• Halogens are very reactive, the reactivity decreases from Fluorine to Astatine.
 
• Physical Properties of Halogens:
 
 
• They have a strong and often nasty smell.
 
• They are extremely toxic.
 
• They are poor conductors of heat and electricity.
 
• They have low melting and boiling points.
 
 
 
• Chemical Properties of Halogens:
 
 
• Their Molecules are diatomic.
 
• They have seven valence electrons as their one electron missing, they form negative ions and are highly reactive.
 
• They can gain an electron by reacting with atoms of other elements.
 
 

 
• **Group 14**, also known as the **Carbon Group**, is a significant part of the p-block in the periodic table. Here are some key points about Group 14:

 
 
• Members: This group includes carbon (C), silicon (Si), germanium (Ge), tin (Sn), lead (Pb), and flerovium (Fl).
 
• Electron Configuration: Each of these elements has only two electrons in its outermost p orbital with the electron configuration of ns2np2.
 
• Chemical Behavior: Group 14 elements show a wide range of chemical behaviors, more so than any other family in the periodic table. Three of the five elements—carbon, tin, and lead—have been known since ancient times.
 
• Oxidation States: The elements of this group typically show an oxidation state of +4, but lower oxidation states are also common, especially for the heavier elements.
 
• Anomalous Behavior of Carbon: Carbon, compared to the other elements in the group, displays distinctly different properties due to its smaller size, higher electronegativity, and absence of d orbitals in its valence shell.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes water transport in plants?

options.text: The process which is the main driving force of water into the xylem during the day is root pressure.
The process in which loss of water takes place in the form of water vapour through stomata is called transpiration.
The process of water loss from stomata requires energy in the form of ATP.
The process by which water is pulled from the xylem cells of the roots into leaves is called translocation.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The process in which loss of water takes place in the form of water vapor through stomata is called transpiration.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **"transpiration"** refers to **the process of removing surplus water from the plant's body**. Water molecules in the plant tissues are removed from the aerial regions of the plants during transpiration.
 
• **Plants** only use a small portion of the water they **absorb for growth and development**. The remainder is expelled through transpiration.90 % of excess water is transpired by **stomata **present in the leaves of the plants.
 
• A very little amount of water is transpired from the stems or barks of the plants with the help of lenticels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **The osmotic balance** of the cell is maintained by the process of transpiration.
 
• **Transpiration **is the unavoidable consequence of gas exchange in the leaf. This is because the plant has to open pores on the leaves called the **stomata.**
 
• When they **open gas exchange **occurs and the plant releases Oxygen as waste while simultaneously absorbing **CO₂ **for use during photosynthesis.
 
• It also helps in the absorption and distribution of water along with minerals from the soil through roots.

questions.question: Two trains are moving in opposite directions at speeds of 80 km/h and 120 km/h. The length of one train time is 300 m. The time taken by them to cross each other is 12 seconds. The length (in m) of the other train, correct to 2 decimal places, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed of trains = 80 + 120 = 200 km/h = 200 × (5/18) = 500/9 m/s.

Total distance covered in 12 seconds = Speed × Time = (500/9) × 12 = 2000/3 m = 666.67 m.

Length of the other train = Total Distance − Length of first train.

Length of the other train = 666.67 − 300 = 366.67 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 366.67 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of first train (S₁) = 80 km/h

Speed of second train (S₂) = 120 km/h

Length of first train (L₁) = 300 m

Time taken to cross each other (T) = 12 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (when moving in opposite directions) = S₁ + S₂

Total Distance = Relative Speed × Time

 
• 
 
 L1 = 300 m
 80 km/h →
 
 L2 = x m
 ← 120 km/h
 Opposite Direction ⇒ Relative Speed = 80 + 120 = 200 km/h
 Time to Cross = 12 s

**Calculation:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 80 + 120 = 200 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 200 × (5/18) = 1000/18 = 500/9 m/s

⇒ Total Distance (L₁ + L₂) = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ 300 + L₂ = (500/9) × 12

⇒ 300 + L₂ = 500 × (4/3) = 2000/3

⇒ L₂ = (2000/3) − 300

⇒ L₂ = (2000 − 900) ÷ 3

⇒ L₂ = 1100 ÷ 3 ≈ 366.67 m

**∴ The correct answer is 366.67 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction with speeds u and v (where u > v), their relative speed is (u − v).

Conversion of Speed Units

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

When a train of length L crosses a stationary point object like a pole or a standing man, the distance covered is exactly equal to the length of the train L. Time taken = L ÷ Speed of the train.

questions.question: Electromagnetic induction is the phenomenon wherein:

options.text: a moving closed loop of a conductor induces an EMF in the closed loop of another conductor

a moving magnet induces an EMF in the closed loop of a conductor
a moving coil carrying current induces force on the magnet

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a moving magnet induces an EMF in the closed loop of a conductor.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phenomenon of electromagnetic induction is the current induced in a coil due to relative motion between a magnet and the coil.
 
• It was discovered by Michael Faraday.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Faraday’s First Law of Electromagnetic Induction:

 
• It states that, "whenever a conductor is placed in a varying magnetic field, an electromotive force is induced. If the conductor circuit is closed, a current is induced, which is called induced current".
 
• The magnetic field intensity in a closed loop can be changed 
 
 
• By rotating the coil relative to the magnet.
 
• By moving the coil into or out of the magnetic field.
 
• By changing the area of a coil placed in the magnetic field.
 
• By moving a magnet towards or away from the coil.
 
 
 

Faraday’s Second Law of Electromagnetic Induction:

 
• It states that, "the induced emf in a coil is equal to the rate of change of flux linkage".
 
• The flux linkage is the product of the number of turns in the coil and the flux associated with the coil.
 
• The formula of Faraday’s 2nd law is given by E = -N(dϕ )/(dt)
 
• Where E is the electromotive force, Φ is the magnetic flux, and N is the number of turns.

questions.question: A, B and C invested Rs. 10,000, Rs. 12,000, and Rs. 15,000, respectively, for 5, 6, and 9 months, respectively, in a business. If A's share in the profit is Rs. 2,500, then the total profit is:
